name: support-triage
domain: Customer support tickets for an online shoe store. Customers write about late or lost deliveries, returns and exchanges, wrong sizes, duplicate or unexpected charges, refunds, discount codes and account access.
state: The ticket exactly as the customer typed it: one to five sentences in the first person. Mix calm, confused and angry customers; some make typos or write in lowercase; a few mention two problems at once.

department.instructions: Which team should handle this ticket first?

criteria.returns: Exchanges, refunds for returned items, wrong or damaged items
criteria.shipping: Delivery status, delays, lost packages, address changes
criteria.billing: Charges, invoices, payment failures, duplicate charges, discount codes
criteria.account: Login problems, password resets, email changes, closing the account

escalate.instructions: Does this ticket need urgent attention from a human within the hour?

guidance: department is the team that must act first: a late delivery that also asks for a refund is shipping until the package is found. escalate is true only for threats to dispute a charge or go to the press, safety issues, orders needed for an event within 48 hours, or a customer who has already written more than once. frustration 2 requires explicit anger, insults, all caps, or a threat to leave; polite complaints are 0 or 1.
variety: length: one short line up to a full paragraph
detail: with and without order numbers, dates, product names
writing: clean prose, lowercase and typos, non-native English, one or two in Spanish or German
ambiguity: tickets that mention two departments but clearly need one first
